tagline: Games, quizzes and one stubborn iOS app.
description: Paj's playground: browser games, anime quizzes, and a devlog about building TAG, an iOS app for a month-long game of real-life tag.
status:
### TAG — where the app is right now

**Stage 3. The build is uploaded and waiting on Apple.** Version 1.0.0 is signed, archived and sitting in App Store Connect. The app record is filled in: name, age rating, and a privacy declaration naming every one of the five things it collects. Next stop is TestFlight, on my own phone.

**The blocker is gone.** The Apple Developer Program was the one thing I had been putting off buying until the app deserved it. It deserved it.

**Push notifications work, on a real phone, all the way through.** Not "the code is written" — an actual notification arrived on an actual iPhone. So did the silent kind: three wake-ups, three fresh positions, seven to eight seconds every time. The even delay is the proof. A single position could have turned up on its own.

Everything from stages 1 and 2 still stands: accounts, gangs with invite codes, GPS-verified tags, the timeline, statistics, the hunt, the map, UAVs, truces, Bluetooth indoors, an album of evidence and a Hall of Shame that remembers every year.

Migrations 1 to 27 are running in production. 66 unit tests, 403 database assertions and four interface tests that play the real game against the real backend.

**Next:** Apple finishes processing the build, then TestFlight. After that the screenshots and the review notes, and then it goes in front of a reviewer.

**Still waiting on two phones:** the Bluetooth side is fully tested on the server and cannot be tested in a simulator, because a simulator has no radio.
